text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging surge detected on runtime cluster r-23 (region us-west-2). Elevated page faults and GPU memory reclaim activity. Auto-tagging oncall.

maria: ack — @jordan are you oncall?

jordan: oncall here, looking. Any customer reports?

customer-success: FYI we got a support ticket at 2024-11-02T03:12Z from AcmeCorp about latency spikes and occasional 503s. A few other prod endpoints reported increased p99.

oncall-bot: Runbook: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/paging-surge — recommended initial mitigations: reduce batch sizes, enable kvcache-eviction, gather gpu mem stats.

lee: grabbing GPU/runtime stats now, attaching a quick snapshot: 
```
GPU0: total=40960MB used=39540MB free=1420MB pages_in=12345 pages_out=9876 oom_count=0
KVCache: entries=4.2M size=29.1GB fragmentation=18% evict_rate=0.2/s
Batching: active_jobs=120 avg_batch=62 seq_len_p50=128 p95=512
Logs: /var/log/runtime/r-23/2024-11-02T03:10:*.log
```

samira: initial hypothesis: heavy long-seq requests + large avg batch causing KV cache growth and fragmentation -> more pagewalks. Suggest immediate mitigations: reduce batch_size from 64 -> 16 for canary, enable kvcache soft-eviction (threshold 75%), and increase reserved headroom on the pool.

jordan: doing canary now: updating policy to batch_size=16 on 10% of pods (canary id can-132).

ev an: canary rolled (can-132). Early metrics show GPU free memory rising ~800MB and pagewalks dropping ~40% in the 2m window.

lee: sharing a short log snippet from canary side showing fewer page faults: 
```
[03:13:02] runtime: mem_page_fault count=123 -> 78 (can-132)
[03:13:12] kvcache: evict triggered, reclaimed 600MB
[03:13:45] gpu: paging_activity reduced
[03:14:05] request id=abc123 latency=210ms (was 980ms)
```

maria: customer-impact timeline (quick): 03:10Z-03:14Z p99 elevated, ~1200 requests affected, one enterprise call reported timeout. We should notify AcmeCorp with mitigation note.

jordan: pinging product-support to prep customer message; also creating incident ticket with initial postmortem link.

opsbot: Created INC-4321, assigned to eng-ml. Postmortem template: https://intranet.redwood/incidents/INC-4321

samira: agreed next steps: (1) keep canary at 10% for 15m and monitor, (2) roll batch_size=16 to 50% if stable, (3) schedule a KV compaction/defrag job for the cluster overnight, (4) long-term: change allocator to reduce fragmentation and add proactive eviction heuristics.

lee: attaching additional diagnostic excerpt (relevant lines):
```
[03:11:58] allocator: chunk_alloc fail->trigger_page_swap
[03:12:01] gc: kv_fragmentation high=22% region=pool-7
[03:12:22] oom_probe: near_oom_signal=false but high_paging=true
```

jevan: quick note - we observed batch-size reduction reduced avg tokens-in-flight by ~45%, which aligns with lower KV pressure.

maria: handoff plan: @lina will take next shift at 03:45Z and own follow-ups: run the defrag job at 04:00Z if cluster stable, coordinate customer comms, and lead RCA write-up.

lina: taking handoff, acknowledged. I'll pick up logs, expand the timeline, and capture any regression tests that might have triggered the long sequences.

jordan: saved mitigations in runbook and added checklist for oncall: reduce batch, enable soft-evict, monitor p99/p95/p50, watch GPU free memory and kv evict rate.

maria: thanks team — immediate mitigation looks effective. We'll convert this to a full RCA doc tomorrow. For now: keep alerting thresholds lowered for 4h and monitor. :thumbsup:
